subject: URGENT: CloudCart production latency + 5xx spike — routing / failover request
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cloudcart.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: URGENT: CloudCart production latency + 5xx spike — routing / failover request

Daniel — saw your alert, thank you for the heads up. We’re seeing a correlated latency surge and a ~12% 5xx rate from requests served out of us-west-2 (AZ-2) starting ~09:02 PT. I’ve attached a quick request trace bundle to this thread (request_trace_1105.zip).

Customers impacted: checkout flows and batch webhook ingestion (high QPS path).

Immediate ask: Can we trigger a cross-region redistribution for this customer to route steady-state traffic to us-west-1 while we investigate the AZ-2 degradation? They’re in heavy production right now and have requested an urgent mitigation.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Shift 30% of CloudCart steady-state traffic to us-west-1 as a safety canary.
- Enable the compat model variant (lower memory/kvs footprint) for CloudCart in us-west-1 to reduce token processing overhead.
- Keep a short rollback window (10m) and monitor error rates and p50/p95 latency.

Sooj, Markus — can you validate routing compatibility and confirm any config we must toggle on the routing layer?

Daniel — I’ll keep you updated live on this thread. If you’d prefer a bridge, we can stand one up (I’ve looped Sean for exec visibility).

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: request_trace_1105.zip

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-05T09:26:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: CloudCart production latency + 5xx spike — routing / failover request

Thanks Chloe — I’m on it. Quick findings from infra side:
- Observed qps spike concentrated in us-west-2 AZ-2 on the inference tier (token-service). Concurrently we see queue depth rising and a small KV-cache pressure event.
- Error fingerprint: 502s coming from model runtime timeouts (slow kernels under peak sequence length); not a network partition.

Immediate mitigation plan I can action now:
1) Apply routing diversion rule to route 30% of CloudCart traffic to us-west-1 (canary).
2) Enable compat-model variant in us-west-1 for CloudCart only (lower-latency config).
3) Apply KV-cache eviction tuning for AZ-2 and reduce per-request token budget temporarily.

I’ll drop a short routing-plan PDF in the thread with the exact steps (routing-plan-v1.pdf). I recommend we hold off on global cutover until the canary is stable for 15 minutes. If canary shows p95 improvement >20% and 5xx <1%, we expand to 70% then full.

I’m standing by to execute now — confirm please.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing-plan-v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-05T09:41:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: CloudCart production latency + 5xx spike — routing / failover request

Looping Sean for exec visibility and fast approvals on prioritization and any commercial remediation (credits / SLA gestures).

Summary for execs: CloudCart (DEAL-7321) is experiencing elevated p95 latency (+180ms) and 5xx rate (~12%) originating from us-west-2 AZ-2. SRE recommends immediate 30% diversion to us-west-1 + compat-model variant for CloudCart only as a canary.

Potential customer impact if not mitigated: failed checkouts and webhook retries leading to larger incident. Given this is a revenue-critical customer, we should be prepared to offer a short one-time credit if this persists beyond the mitigation window.

Sean — can you confirm we can greenlight the diversion and approve an on-call escalation budget if additional GPU capacity/priority is required? I’ll coordinate communications to CloudCart once we have the diversion underway.

—Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cloudcart.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cloudcart.com
Date: 2028-11-05T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: CloudCart production latency + 5xx spike — routing / failover request

Chloe, Soojin — appreciate the quick investigation and proposed plan. Checkout errors started showing at 09:05 PT and we started throttling non-essential background jobs. Please confirm ETA for the 30% diversion and what end-user window we should expect for stabilization. Also please advise whether a public status update to our ops channel is recommended (we’ll coordinate on our side).

Regarding compensation — we’ll wait for the mitigation and then revisit if there’s an extended degradation window. For visibility, we have one major marketplace partner running high-volume checkouts; any ETA helps.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudCart

On Nov 5, 2028, at 09:12, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Daniel — saw your alert, thank you for the heads up. We’re seeing a correlated latency surge and a ~12% 5xx rate from requests served out of us-west-2 (AZ-2) starting ~09:02 PT. I’ve attached a quick request trace bundle to this thread (request_trace_1105.zip).

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cloudcart.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-05T13:04:00Z
Subject: ACTIONED: 30% diversion live (us-west-1 canary) — monitoring + next steps

Update: We’ve executed the 30% diversion to us-west-1 canary at 12:52 PT. Early signal (10m): p95 down ~28%, 5xx dropped to 0.8% on canary cohort. us-west-2 AZ-2 still degraded; SRE is applying the KV-cache eviction tweaks and monitoring kernel-level stalls.

Next steps / timeline:
- 12:52–13:10 PT: canary stabilisation window (monitoring ongoing).
- If canary holds (p95 improvement >20% and 5xx <1%), expand diversion to 70% at ~13:20 PT.
- Prepare full cutover and post-incident RCA after stabilisation.

I’ve opened a bridge (support.redwood/bridges/cc-1105) and posted the runbook link for internal ops. We’ll keep CloudCart updated every 15 minutes; Markus will handle external exec comms if we need to discuss credits.

Thanks team — great quick execution.

Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
